title: Cigarroa Says She Will Skip Nov. 18 Mayoral Debate, Citing Fairness Concerns
excerpt: Mayoral candidate and District 8 Councilwoman Alyssa Cigarroa announced Tuesday night she will not take part in the Nov. 18 debate hosted by the City of Laredo, saying she has concerns about the fairness and impartiality of the city-run event. She said she will take part in a Dec. 8 debate hosted by the Laredo Chamber of Commerce and airing on KGNS.
content:
Mayoral candidate and District 8 Councilwoman Alyssa Cigarroa announced Tuesday night, Nov. 17, that she will not take part in the Nov. 18 debate hosted by the City of Laredo, citing concerns about fairness and impartiality.

In her announcement, Cigarroa said the city has shown preferential treatment toward incumbent Mayor Dr. Victor Treviño, including through its official social media platforms, and argued the circumstances raised serious concerns about the city’s ability to conduct a fair and impartial debate, according to the report. Webb Watch has not independently verified those claims, and the announcement did not provide specific examples of how the Nov. 18 debate’s questions, moderation or rules would favor either candidate, according to the report.

Cigarroa previously missed the Oct. 8 city-hosted mayoral forum, reportedly because of a prior engagement. She did take part in the Oct. 7 Chamber of Commerce forum and the Oct. 14 TAMIU debate, according to The Bridge, the Texas A&M International University student newspaper.

Comments were reportedly disabled on Cigarroa’s announcement, preventing residents from responding publicly beneath the post. The restriction is particularly noteworthy given that her statement emphasized listening to Laredoans, answering their questions and remaining accessible to the community.

Despite withdrawing from the Nov. 18 event, Cigarroa said she will participate in the Dec. 8 debate hosted by the Laredo Chamber of Commerce and airing on KGNS, according to the report.

Treviño and Cigarroa face off in a mayoral runoff on Dec. 12 after no candidate won more than 50 percent of the vote on Nov. 3, with early voting running Nov. 30 through Dec. 8, according to KGNS.

Update — Nov. 18, 2026: The city-hosted debate went ahead as planned on Wednesday, Nov. 18, despite Cigarroa’s withdrawal, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

Update — Nov. 18, 2026, evening: The City of Laredo streamed the forum live on its Facebook page Wednesday evening as part of Laredo Votes 2026, the city's nonpartisan voter education initiative, ahead of the Dec. 12 runoff. When Webb Watch checked the stream, about 20 minutes in, the broadcast was still showing opening title cards, with no candidates speaking yet.

Update — Nov. 18, 2026, later in the evening: The City of Laredo later posted a wrap-up of the forum, saying it was held Wednesday evening as part of Laredo Votes 2026 and thanking residents who attended in person and tuned in online. The city said it remains committed to nonpartisan voter education ahead of the Dec. 12 runoff.

Update — Nov. 18, 2026, evening: Former mayoral candidate JD Gonzalez appeared at Wednesday's forum in support of Mayor Treviño. Gonzalez, who finished third in the Nov. 3 election, had already endorsed Treviño in the runoff.

Update — Nov. 21, 2026: The Laredo Chamber of Commerce forum between Cigarroa and Treviño has been moved up to Wednesday, Dec. 2, and is set to air live at 6:30 p.m. on KGNS-TV 8 and KGNS+. It had previously been scheduled for Dec. 8, the final day of early voting. The Dec. 2 date falls on the third day of early voting, which runs Nov. 30 through Dec. 8. Cigarroa’s earlier announcement promoting the Dec. 8 date no longer appears on her social media page, and a new announcement promoting Dec. 2 has appeared in its place. No in-person location for the Dec. 2 forum has been announced.

Sources: City of Laredo, Facebook, Nov. 18, 2026; City of Laredo, Facebook (forum recap), Nov. 18, 2026.
